solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They can become restless for oysters

definitions.meaning: from the saying that the locals, the indigenous people, are getting restless when a crowd turns unruly
a native is an oyster raised in an artificial bed, especially a British one

explanation.surface: A wry remark about people who may grow restless, paired oddly with shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half alludes to the stock phrase 'the natives are getting restless'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the shellfish trade, natives are oysters bred in British beds, a specialist sense of the word.

clue.text: Tie-dyed fabric found regularly in pink pants

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the words that follow, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A tie-dyed material spotted in a pair of pink trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of 'pink pants' gives the fabric's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikat is a textile made by resist-dyeing threads before weaving, a tie-dye technique.

clue.text: Note Chelsea's side in Emirates after November showing a subtle difference

indicators.note: after puts the Emirates construction behind the November letter

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in places the note and Chelsea's edge letter within the Emirates abbreviation

parts.note: UAE is the United Arab Emirates

indicators.note: side here means the edge, the opening letter of Chelsea

explanation.surface: A football picture: Chelsea playing at the Emirates, Arsenal's ground, in November.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emirates Stadium is Arsenal's London ground, but here it is the country, UAE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of distinction in meaning, tone or colour.

clue.text: Nothing short of a nutty sweet 16

definitions.note: a cross-reference to the answer at 16-down, a drink taken before a meal; this liqueur is one

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the nothing is dropped from what follows

parts.note: a noisette is a hazelnut chocolate
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A seemingly breathless verdict that some sweet sixteen-year-old is downright crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing short of' reads as an intensifier but tells you to remove O. '16' is not an age; it points to 16-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette, an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, is commonly served as a pre-dinner drink, the sense of 16-down.

clue.text: Knot separated with difficulty

parts.note: clove is a past tense of cleave, to split apart
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A tangle that was pulled apart only with great effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a common sailor's knot used to fasten a rope to a post.

clue.text: They have the gall all right to incarcerate a lunatic

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up, so the outer piece holds the a inside it

parts.note: OK means all right
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Somebody has the nerve to lock up a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gall' looks like cheek, but means a growth on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak nuts are galls, the round growths insects cause on oak trees, so they literally have galls.

clue.text: Evangelist known to reveal destiny?

parts.note: Mark is one of the four Gospel writers
out means revealed or public, as a secret that is out

explanation.surface: A gospel writer is said to disclose what fate holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark out someone is to single them out as destined for something, showing their future.

clue.text: Contaminated carbuncle a nasty case

indicators.note: case says the letters are held inside the casing of the words carbuncle a nasty

explanation.surface: A doctor's note: an infected boil, a really unpleasant instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a medical case but tells you the answer is encased in the preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean is dirty or impure, the state of being contaminated.

clue.text: Protects jobs they traditionally hold down

definitions.meaning: to featherbed is to protect workers by keeping unnecessary staff or practices
old mattresses were stuffed with feathers, so they contain down

explanation.surface: A comment on job protection that traditionally keeps wages or workers held down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is not oppression but soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbedding is overmanning to secure employment; feather beds are mattresses filled with plumage.

clue.text: Vessels circle and stick soundly in shifting silt

parts.note: O is the shape of a circle

indicators.note: in says the fastening word goes inside the rearranged silt
shifting means the letters of silt move about
soundly says the word is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: anchor means to fix or stick fast

explanation.surface: Ships run aground, circling and getting stuck in shifting silt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' and 'soundly' both signal changes; 'soundly' looks like 'firmly', but it means stick is taken only as heard, a word for fasten a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil tankers are large ships built to carry petroleum, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Five for fifty in fast opening

indicators.note: Five for fifty means one numeral swaps in where the other stood

parts.note: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter
L is fifty in Roman numerals
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something like a quick swap of numbers at the start of a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast opening' looks like a quick start, but 'fast' is Lent and 'opening' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an aperture through which air or gas escapes.

clue.text: In-form favourite, lacking runs and training, makes case for move

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the runs and training are removed

parts.note: a teacher's pet is the favourite in a school form, or class
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
PE is physical education, training at school

explanation.surface: A sporting favourite in good form, short of runs and practice, puts up a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In-form' is not about good form; a form is a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea chests, the wooden crates tea was shipped in, are classic boxes for packing when moving house.

clue.text: Crush strike gripping North? Sure thing's short answer

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the striking word surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: to coin is to strike money, as at a mint
N is North
a cert is a certainty, a sure thing
A is short for answer

explanation.surface: A tale of a union strike grip in the North, with a sure-thing result.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Sure thing's' is 'is' joining CERT to the pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To concertina is to fold up or crush like the bellows of the squeezebox instrument.

clue.text: French film-maker capturing essence of chic island

indicators.note: capturing means holding, so the director's name goes around the core of chic

parts.note: Jacques Tati made Monsieur Hulot's Holiday

indicators.note: essence means the heart, the middle letters of chic

explanation.surface: A French director filming something stylish on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Fights for jobs

definitions.meaning: battles between forces, as military clashes
bookings for work, as a performer's gigs

explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a battle; it is also a hired appointment, as a musician's booked performance.

clue.text: A tire pressure's raised if it leads to blow-out

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read from the bottom up, so tire and pressure are backwards

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A motoring warning: tyre pressure going up can lead to a burst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TIREP into PERIT. 'Blow-out' is not a burst tyre but a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before a feast, so it precedes a lavish meal.

clue.text: One boob breaking vase and he's white-faced at work

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the vase is cut apart by the other pieces

parts.note: a pot is a vessel such as a vase
I is the Roman numeral one
to boob is to blunder, to err

explanation.surface: Someone blunders, breaks a vase and goes pale at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the stock pantomime clown who performs with whitened face.

clue.text: Straight line cried out for old ruler

indicators.note: cried out says the words are spoken, so the phrase is matched by its sound

parts.note: fair means straight or honest, and a row is a line

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a straight line in honour of an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent FAIR ROW sounds like the ruler's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The pharaohs were kings of ancient Egypt, rulers of long ago.

clue.text: Guy with appreciation for steak

parts.note: to guy is to tease, as to rib someone
an eye is an appreciation, as in an eye for beauty

explanation.surface: A man who appreciates a good steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is a verb meaning mock, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib-eye is a beef cut from the rib section, a popular steak.

clue.text: Ditch order for tea before there's a rumpus

indicators.note: before puts the tea word ahead of the ditch
an order for tea is called out, so the informal word for a cuppa is taken by sound

parts.note: brew is an informal word for a cup of tea
a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a boundary fence in a landscaped garden

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their tea order and a row breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb, but it is the ha-ha, a sunken boundary on British country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or fuss, a near synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Painter taking last month off — he can talk

indicators.note: taking with off means removing, so the month is subtracted
off with taking signals the month is dropped from the painter

parts.note: a decorator paints houses
DEC is December, the final month of the year

explanation.surface: A painter who took December off can certainly chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' suggests an artist but is a house decorator.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, someone skilled in delivering speeches.

clue.text: A proportion of nostalgia-mongers thrived in the past

indicators.note: proportion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people who trade in nostalgia flourished back in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic word for formerly, once, long ago.

clue.text: A staple of Bollywood banality?

parts.note: maize is a staple grain, and corn also means trite sentimentality, which Indian cinema can supply

explanation.surface: A dig at clichés that Mumbai films rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a staple food it is maize; read as cheesiness it is the hackneyed corn of Hindi cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: This is maize, a staple cereal, and corn also means hackneyed sentiment, here from India.

clue.text: Composer's pen

definitions.meaning: John ..., the American avant-garde composer of 4'33"
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.definitionFit: John Cage was a US experimental composer; an animal enclosure with bars is a pen.

clue.text: One keeping shoes on losing time in muddy biathlon

indicators.note: muddy means messed up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
losing means the time letter is dropped from biathlon

explanation.surface: A competitor who keeps shoes on despite losing time in a muddy biathlon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops T to leave BIAHLON, which 'muddy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobnail is a heavy-headed nail in boot soles, so it helps keep the sole on the shoe.

clue.text: Permanently pro-Right

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
right as a noun means what is good, virtue

explanation.definitionFit: Something done for good is done forever, never to be reversed.
